body:
Under Ind AS 115 / ASC 606, revenue recognised before the right to bill becomes a **contract asset**. Under Ind AS presentation it is also called "unbilled revenue". If only the passage of time stands between the company and the cash, it is an unbilled **receivable**. Unbilled revenue is the riskiest receivable: the customer has not yet accepted an invoice.

**Worked example G: Infosys vs Wipro. IFRS 20-F XBRL.**

| | Infosys FY23 | Infosys FY25 | Wipro FY23 | Wipro FY25 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $18,212 m | $19,277 m | ₹90,488 cr | ₹89,088 cr |
| Trade receivables | 3,094 | 3,645 | 12,635 | 11,775 |
| Accrued income / contract assets | 2,037 | 1,764 | 2,300 | 1,580 |
| Billed DSO | 62 d | 69 d | 51 d | 48 d |
| Unbilled days | 41 d | 33 d | 9 d | 6 d |
| **Total DSO** | **103 d** | **102 d** | **60 d** | **55 d** |

- Infosys carries about a month of revenue as unbilled. That is structural (fixed-price and milestone contracts), and it is stable, so it is not a flag.
- Wipro's unbilled balance fell by a third. Contract assets shrinking while revenue is flat is a sign of **cleaner** quality, not worse.
- **The flag:** unbilled days rising for 2+ years while billed DSO is also rising. In EPC, add "contract assets net of contract liabilities (customer advances)" and track it against the order book.

body:
- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:US-CRM:initial-fy28-revenue-guide-10pct-plus`
- **Method:** promise-tracker credibility · **P(ours)** 0.30 · **P(base)** 0.25 · resolve by 2027-03-15
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 release (26-Aug-2026): revenue $11.3bn (+11%, incl. $456m Informatica), subscription & support +12%; cRPO $33.5bn (+14%); FY27 revenue guide raised by $200m to $46.1–46.4bn (+11–12%); CFO Washington: 'NNAOV growth is the strongest it's been in four years, keeping us on track for second-half organic revenue reacceleration'; Agentforce + Data 360 ARR ~$3.9bn (+210%); Contentful and Fin acquisitions expected to close in Q3 FY27. Yahoo: CRM $180.62 on 20-Nov-2026 (52-wk $146–269).
- **Why our number differs from base:** Promise-tracker: management has promised organic reacceleration. FY28 loses most of the Informatica inorganic boost (deal laps during FY27), so a ≥10% guide needs either real organic acceleration (cRPO +14% hints at it) or meaningful Contentful/Fin contribution. Salesforce's recent initial guides have been 7–9% (from memory, unverified). We go slightly above the base because cRPO is leading revenue.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Naive: Salesforce initial annual guides in FY25–FY27 implied high-single-digit growth except when padded by acquisitions; ≥10% ~25%.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if (midpoint of the initial FY28 revenue guidance range in Salesforce's Q4 FY27 release ÷ FY27 reported revenue) − 1 ≥ 10.0%. Use reported (not constant-currency) figures.
- **Resolution source:** Salesforce Q4 FY27 earnings release (8-K, EDGAR)
- **Sources used:** https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1108524/000110852426000187/crm-q2fy27xexhibit991.htm; https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/CRM
- **Confidence of evidence:** single-source

`tools/promise_tracker/pipeline` has no SEC fetcher (README v1.3: US ledgers are built by hand from Ex-99.1 releases). Ledger:
| # | Made | Promise | Outcome | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 31-Jul-25 | FY25 EPS growth 15–25% ("closer to the lower end" if softness persists) | +15.9% on adj 5.46 → 6.33 | delivered (low end) |
| 2 | 31-Jul-25 | Inland Q3 utilization "low 90% range" | mid-80% | **missed** |
| 3 | 31-Jul-25 | Inland margins "remain in the 20% range" | Q3 high-teens; Q4 low-20s | **missed** |
| 4 | 31-Jul-25 | Coastal margins mid-to-high teens, modest H2 improvement | ~20% in Q3 and Q4 | delivered (beat) |
| 5 | 31-Jul-25 | KDS FY revenue flat to slightly up, high-single-digit margin | +5.6%, 9.2% | delivered (beat) |
| 6 | 31-Jul-25 | CFO $620–720M | $670.2M | delivered |
| 7 | 31-Jul-25 | Capex $260–290M | $264.5M | delivered |
| 8 | 29-Oct-25 | Q4 inland revenue *and* margins improve modestly vs Q3 | margin up (high-teens → low-20s); revenue ≈ flat (79% × 481.7 vs 80% × 484.9) | partly |
| 9 | 29-Oct-25 | Coastal Q4 revenue and margins comparable to Q3 | ~20% margin; revenue +4% | delivered |
| 10 | 29-Oct-25 | KDS FY revenue up mid-single digits, high-single-digit margins | +5.6%, 9.2% | delivered |
| 11 | 29-Jan-26 | Q1-26 the lowest-margin quarter of 2026 | Q1 12.8% vs Q2 13.3%, Q3 15.4% | delivered |
| 12 | 28-Oct-26 | $115M barge/fleeting acquisition to close in Q4-26 | closed 4-Nov-2026 | delivered |
| open | 29-Jan-26 → | FY26 EPS growth 0–12% → 5–15% (Apr) → "upper end" (Jul) → 10–15%, "upper end" (Oct) | 9M +13.4% | open (resolves Feb-2027; call 1) |
| open | 29-Jan-26 | Inland FY revenue +low-to-mid single digits → raised to low-double-digit | tracking above | open |
| open | 29-Jan-26 | Coastal margins high-teens → cut to mid-teens (Oct) | tracking below | open (likely miss) |
| open | 29-Jan-26 | KDS revenue flat-to-slightly up → high-single digits | tracking above | open |
| open | 29-Jan-26 | CFO $575–675M; capex $220–260M (unchanged in all four releases) | 9M CFO $313M; capex $189M | open (call 4) |
**Score:** credit (delivered 1, partly 0.5) = 9.5 / 12 = **79%** vs the US-industrials peer median of **84%**
(`insight:us-industrials-promise-credibility-base-rate`: WTS 100, AOS 65.9, SSD 79.4, LECO 88.5; different sector). **Pattern (same as the US
peers):** company-level financial ranges are met or beaten, because guidance starts low and is then raised (2026: three raises). The misses
are operating-condition calls (utilization and inland margins in a soft Q3-25). **Team:** the CEO (Grzebinski, since 2014) and the CFO
(Kumar) are unchanged, so the whole ledger belongs to one team.
